data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"An adaptive perturbation of the regular 4x3 grid, where each point is displaced from its lattice position by a deterministic perturbation vector, achieves minimum triangle area ~0.043 by breaking collinearities while maintaining near-uniform spacing.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If perturbations are too large, inter-point distances shrink and other triangles become minimum.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If perturbations are too small, near-collinear triples still produce very small areas.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the center point aligns with any perturbed grid pair, a zero-area triangle forms.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Start with a 4x3 grid at spacing 1/3, then apply small perturbations (up to 0.05) to each point to break the collinearity that plagues regular grids. The 13th point goes at the center. The perturbation is chosen so that the minimum triangle (originally zero on grid lines) becomes the area of a triangle spanning two adjacent grid cells with perturbation-induced displacement. The key insight is that the optimal perturbation maximizes the minimum deviation from collinearity.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
